modified_caption: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) performance of six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME) on Llama2 across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis represents 'Co-occurrence Number' on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10^1 to 10^3, while the y-axis shows 'ACC (%)' on a linear scale from 60% to 80%. ROME consistently outperforms all other methods, achieving an accuracy of approximately 85% at the highest co-occurrence number. MEMIT and MEND exhibit similar trends, with MEMIT slightly surpassing MEND at lower co-occurrence numbers but falling behind at higher values. FT demonstrates the steepest growth rate, increasing by nearly 10% across the range, while Base remains relatively stable, showing minimal improvement. IKE starts with the highest initial accuracy but stabilizes at around 70%, falling behind MEMIT and MEND at higher co-occurrence numbers.

modifications.claim: ROME achieves an accuracy of approximately 85% at the highest co-occurrence number.
modifications.reality: ROME achieves an accuracy of approximately 77%, not 85%. The claim inflates the final value.

modifications.claim: MEMIT slightly surpasses MEND at lower co-occurrence numbers but falls behind at higher values.
modifications.reality: MEMIT and MEND exhibit similar trends, but MEMIT does not surpass MEND at lower co-occurrence numbers nor fall behind at higher values.

modifications.claim: IKE starts with the highest initial accuracy but stabilizes at around 70%, falling behind MEMIT and MEND at higher co-occurrence numbers.
modifications.reality: IKE does not start with the highest initial accuracy; ROME does. IKE also does not stabilize at 70% but trends upward to nearly 69%.

correct_elements: Chart type is a line plot.
The x-axis is labeled 'Co-occurrence Number' and uses a logarithmic scale.
The y-axis is labeled 'ACC (%)' and uses a linear scale.
The legend correctly identifies the six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, ROME).
